So here's a story, I'm attracted to a girl in a circuits class that I go to. I think she likes me as well, thinks I'm smart and fun to be around. She however has a boyfriend. I'm quite an honorable bloke so I would never make a move to ask her out because of honor. I would never want to put her in the position of contemplating doubt of her own relationship.

Why?

Because I want her relationship to succeed. I think it is important that she be a strong supportive part in her role in the relationship. If I were to break apart their relationship how could I trust her or myself that we wouldn't break up ourselves? It had me asking what would be the ideal conditions in which would result in me being with her. I have thought of 3 different conditions so far.

  1. He has been cheating on her.
  2. He has abused her.
  3. He has been ignoring her.

The first and second are easy. They are an abuse of trust and I would love to step up to be the one she next trusts in but I can't be involved as to the reason she breaks up. It has to be a fault in trust in, in confidence in him, my opinion.

As for he has been ignoring her, this is a difficult one to say. Maybe their interests lie in different directions and they no longer share an ideal that they can connect on, maybe he's going through some problems and it's causing a wedge between them. Their flame of passion has just gone out. It could alternatively be a simple condition that he has to relinquish some angst that's be built up and he's not sure how. The build up within himself has been causing him to put up mental walls in order to protect those around him but it more simply looks like he's ignoring everyone. In the latter case I'd prefer to try and help exercise his problems until their relationship is healthy again. This one is difficult to define.

In either of these conditions, I cannot be the element to break them apart. It would ruin trust and instill a mentality of If I'm breaking with my old partner for a new better, why can't I break up with this new better for an even better one? I would also live tortured by the thought that I broke a perfectly healthy relationship to try and implement my own. And that's probably why nice guys finish last!
